Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction based on a Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot Model.

Source: R/eblup_stfh.R
eblup_stfh.Rd

This function gives the Spatio-Temporal Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (EBLUP) under normality based on a spatio-temporal Fay-Herriot model. It reimplements the same Fisher-scoring algorithm as eblupSTFH() (package sae, Marhuenda, Molina & Morales 2013), but the estimation loop runs in compiled C++/Armadillo, making it substantially faster and more memory-efficient than the original R implementation – especially for a large number of domains/time periods.

Usage

eblup_stfh(
  formula,
  vardir,
  data,
  domain,
  time,
  W,
  model = c("ST", "S"),
  maxiter = 100,
  precision = 1e-04,
  sigma21_start = NULL,
  rho1_start = 0.5,
  sigma22_start = NULL,
  rho2_start = 0.5,
  compute_mse = FALSE,
  mse_type = c("analytical", "bootstrap"),
  B = 100,
  n_threads = 1,
  seed = -1,
  self_benchmark = FALSE,
  benchmark_weight = NULL,
  benchmark_target = NULL,
  benchmark_group = NULL,
  print_result = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

an object of class formula describing the model to fit (response ~ auxiliary variables). Variables must be present in data.

vardir

vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing a column in data, with the sampling variances of the direct estimator. Must be positive in the sampled cells; it is ignored (may be NA) where the response is NA.

data

a data frame (or extension) with one row per domain and time period (domain * time rows), including the cells without a direct estimate: for those, the response (and vardir) is NA, while the auxiliary variables must be available (see Details). Rows may be in any order: they are sorted internally into the domain-major order required by the model (domains in order of first appearance, periods increasing), and the results are returned in the original row order. Note that sae::eblupSTFH() instead assumes a complete panel already in domain-major order.

domain

vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing a domain names column in data. If NULL, the domains are numbered consecutively.

time

vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing a time names column in data.

W

a square proximity/spatial weights matrix of dimension domain x domain (row-standardized, values typically in \([0,1]\)), with rows and columns in the order in which the domains first appear in data. It must cover all domains, including the ones that are never sampled: do not drop them from W, since their predictions borrow strength from their neighbours through it.

model

character, either "ST" (spatio-temporal, default) or "S" (spatial only, no AR(1) temporal component).

maxiter

maximum number of Fisher-scoring iterations. Default 100.

precision

convergence tolerance for the Fisher-scoring algorithm. Default 1e-4.

sigma21_start, rho1_start, sigma22_start, rho2_start

starting values for the variance/autocorrelation components. Defaults mirror eblupSTFH(): 0.5 * median(vardir) for the variances and 0.5 for the autocorrelations. rho2_start is ignored when model = "S". The REML fit first uses the same Fisher-scoring iteration as sae::eblupSTFH(); if that fails (typically a variance iterate turns negative and the covariance matrix becomes indefinite) it falls back to constrained REML (variances \(\ge 0\), \(|\rho| \le 0.999\)) with step halving. When a variance is estimated at 0, its autocorrelation is not identified and its standard error is reported as NA.

compute_mse

logical, if TRUE computes MSE. Default FALSE.

mse_type

character, method for MSE estimation: "analytical" (fast Prasad-Rao type estimator g1 + g2 + 2 g3 - g4, default when compute_mse = TRUE; g3 uses the exact derivative of the EBLUP, \(\Psi P V_a P y\), and the REML information at the final estimates; correlations estimated on the boundary \(|\rho| \ge 0.999\) are treated as fixed, so they do not enter \(g_3\)/\(g_4\)) or "bootstrap" (parametric bootstrap in which the variance components are re-estimated by REML in every replicate, as in Marhuenda et al., 2013).

B

number of bootstrap replicates for MSE computation. Only used when compute_mse = TRUE and mse_type = "bootstrap". Default 100.

n_threads

number of threads for parallel bootstrap MSE computation. Use 0 for all available cores. Default 1.

seed

random seed for bootstrap. Use -1 for no seed. Default -1.

self_benchmark

Logical. If TRUE, fits a self-benchmarking model via the augmented model approach (Wang, Fuller, and Qu, 2008; Rao and Molina, 2015, Sec 10.5.1), ensuring that the weighted aggregate of small area estimates automatically matches the direct survey aggregate or specified benchmark targets without post-hoc adjustment.

benchmark_weight

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the domain benchmarking weights in data (e.g. population sizes or shares). Defaults to equal weights.

benchmark_target

Optional numeric scalar or named vector specifying fixed aggregate benchmark target(s). If NULL (default), calibrates to the weighted aggregate of the direct estimates.

benchmark_group

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the grouping / stratum column in data (e.g. time period / year) for group-specific self-benchmarking.

print_result

print the estimated coefficients or not. Default TRUE.

Value

A list with the same structure as seblup_area(), with additional estvarcomp for spatio-temporal variance/autocorrelation components:

estcoef

data frame with beta, std.error, tvalue, pvalue, as in sae::eblupSTFH(), plus stderr_beta and zvalue (copies, for the column names of the other fastsae models). The p-values use the normal distribution, so tvalue is a z-statistic.

estvarcomp

data frame with estimate, std.error for sigma21, rho1, sigma22, rho2.

goodness

named vector: loglikelihood, the full Gaussian log-likelihood at the REML estimates (as loglike in sae::eblupSTFH()), and AIC and BIC computed from it. The restricted (REML) likelihood is not reported: it depends on the covariates through X, so it cannot compare models with different covariates.

df_eblup

data frame with domain, time, y, eblup, vardir, mse, rse, random_effect_u1, random_effect_u2 and sampled (FALSE for the cells predicted without a direct estimate).

When compute_mse = FALSE, mse and rse are NA.
model

model type ("ST" or "S").

convergence

logical, whether the algorithm converged.

n_iter

number of iterations.

B

number of bootstrap replicates (only when compute_mse = TRUE and mse_type = "bootstrap").

Details

Estimation method. The variance components are estimated by REML only, as in Marhuenda, Molina and Morales (2013) and sae::eblupSTFH(), which derive the Fisher-scoring algorithm, the analytical MSE and the bootstrap for REML; there is no method argument. The standard errors of the variance components are those of sae::eblupSTFH(): the inverse REML information of the last Fisher-scoring iteration.

Unsampled domains and missing periods. Cells whose response is NA (a domain without a sample in some period, or in every period) are not dropped. The model is defined on the full \(D \times T\) grid: the SAR effect \(u_1\) lives on all \(D\) domains of W and the AR(1) effect \(u_2\) on all \(T\) periods. The variance components are estimated by REML from the sampled cells, i.e. from the marginal likelihood with the missing cells integrated out (missing at random), and every cell gets the best linear unbiased predictor of \(x_{dt}'\beta + u_{1d} + u_{2dt}\) given the sampled data (Saei and Chambers, 2005; Benedetti et al., 2024 for the spatial effect): $$\tilde\theta_{dt} = x_{dt}'\tilde\beta + a_{dt}' V^{-1} (y - X\tilde\beta),$$ with \(a_{dt}\) the covariance between the cell and the sampled direct estimates. A missing period of a sampled domain borrows from the other periods of the domain (AR(1)) and from the neighbours (SAR); a domain that is never sampled is predicted from its neighbours only (spatial kriging). With model = "S" the period effect of a missing cell is independent of the data, so only the spatial part is borrowed.

MSE. For sampled cells the analytical MSE is \(g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 - g_4\) (Marhuenda et al., 2013). For the cells predicted without a direct estimate it is \(g_1 + g_2 + g_3\), where \(g_1\) and \(g_2\) are the MSE of the predictor with known variance components and \(g_3\) comes from the exact derivative of the predictor in those components (g4 is 0 for these cells). The further second-order correction of the plug-in \(g_1\) is not applied: it is numerically unstable when \(\rho_1\) approaches \(\pm 1\) or a variance component is weakly identified, while in simulations \(g_1 + g_2 + g_3\) has a relative bias of a few percent and close to nominal coverage for these cells. The parametric bootstrap generates the random effects on the full grid and the sampling errors on the sampled cells, re-estimates the model on the sampled cells and predicts every cell, so it covers both kinds of cells. The auxiliary variables must be known for every cell, since they enter the prediction. Self-benchmarking calibrates the weighted aggregate of the sampled cells of each group.

References

  1. Marhuenda, Y., Molina, I., & Morales, D. (2013). Small area estimation with spatio-temporal Fay-Herriot models. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 58, 308-325.

  2. Rao, J. N., & Molina, I. (2015). Small area estimation. John Wiley & Sons.

  3. Saei, A., & Chambers, R. (2005). Out of sample estimation for small areas using area level data. Southampton Statistical Sciences Research Institute, Methodology Working Paper M05/11.

  4. Benedetti, R., Piersimoni, F., Pratesi, M., Salvati, N., & Suesse, T. (2024). Handling out-of-sample areas to estimate the unemployment rate at local labour market areas in Italy. International Statistical Review. doi:10.1111/insr.12596

Examples

library(fastsae)

# mys_panel: 42 domains x 11 years; domains 21 and 25 are never sampled (y = NA).
# They stay in the data and in W, and are predicted from their neighbours.
m1 <- eblup_stfh(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
  data = mys_panel,
  vardir = ~vardir,
  domain = ~area,
  time = ~year,
  W = mys_proxmat,
  model = "ST"
)
#> ℹ Predicting 22 cells without a direct estimate: 2 unsampled domains (spatial borrowing) and 0 missing periods of sampled domains.
#> 
#> ── Fast Small Area Estimation (fastsae) ────────────────────────────────────────
#> Call:
#> eblup_stfh(formula = y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, vardir = ~vardir, data = mys_panel,
#> domain = ~area, time = ~year, W = mys_proxmat, model = "ST")
#> 
#> ✔ Convergence: Yes (in 6 iterations)
#> Model: Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot (SAR + AR(1) time effects)
#> Method: REML
#> Cells without a direct estimate: 22 of 462 (predicted from the model)

# Analytical MSE for every cell, sampled or not
m2 <- eblup_stfh(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3,
  data = mys_panel,
  vardir = ~vardir,
  domain = ~area,
  time = ~year,
  W = mys_proxmat,
  model = "ST",
  compute_mse = TRUE,
  mse_type = "analytical"
)
